get.description: Newest first. `action` matches by prefix, so `user.` returns every action on users. Filter by acting user, entity, or time range. Sensitive values are masked at write time and never present to be returned.
`oldValues` and `newValues` are JSON objects of the properties that changed.
get.summary: One entry with its before/after values

post.description: Requires the current password. Rotates the security stamp and revokes every refresh token, including the caller's — the client must sign in again.

Returns a short-lived access token in the body and sets the rotating refresh token as an httpOnly cookie. Rate-limited per client IP; repeated failures lock the account for the configured lockout period.
post.summary: Sign in with email and password

post.description: Idempotent: succeeds whether or not a valid refresh cookie was presented.

get.description: The single source the frontend gates its UI from. Permissions here are advisory for display only — the API enforces them independently on every call.
get.summary: The signed-in user and their effective permissions

post.description: Rotates the refresh token: the presented token is revoked and replaced. Presenting an already-rotated token is treated as a leak and revokes the rest of that rotation chain.
post.summary: Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token

get.description: Paged and filterable. `search` matches name, slug, and owner email; `status` filters on Provisioning, Active, Suspended, or Deleted; `country` filters on ISO alpha-2. Deleted gyms are excluded unless `includeDeleted=true`, so a deleted tenant is never counted in a figure someone reports upward. `pageSize` is capped server-side.

post.description: The gym is created in Provisioning: set up — branding, staff — before members can reach it, then `activate` when it opens. The slug is permanent and is never reused, including by a deleted gym, because it appears in URLs members may still have. Returns the created gym and its `ETag`, so no follow-up GET is needed.

delete.description: Requires the `X-Confirm-Action` header carrying the gym's slug (AD-6): this removes an entire business's access, so a mis-clicked row in a list must not be able to do it. The row survives the retention window so invoices and audit entries stay readable; a purge job performs the hard delete. Terminal — there is no undelete. Repeating the call on an already-deleted gym succeeds. `GET` the gym afterwards to see the recorded deletion.

get.description: A soft-deleted gym still resolves here, deliberately: an operator investigating why a tenant stopped working needs to see that it was deleted and when. Subscription, resolved features, device summary, and aggregate stats arrive with the modules that own them (M3–M6) rather than as fields that always read zero.

put.description: Slug is not editable — it is the gym's public address and the confirmation phrase for deletion. Requires `If-Match` carrying the `rowVersion` you read: without it the request is refused with 428, and a stale version with 409. Returns the updated gym and its new `ETag`.

post.description: The deliberate moment a gym goes live. Only a gym in Provisioning can be activated: a suspended gym goes through `reactivate`, which is a different decision and a different permission. `If-Match` is honored when supplied but not required — the lifecycle transition rules already refuse the unsafe orderings. Returns the updated gym.
post.summary: Open a provisioned gym for business

put.description: Declarative: send the complete branding, and an omitted value is cleared. A custom domain must be unique across the platform. Requires `If-Match` carrying the gym's `rowVersion` — branding is part of the gym's representation and shares its version, so a successful branding change also moves the gym's `ETag`. Returns the updated gym.

post.description: Returns the gym to Active and clears the suspension reason. Only a suspended gym can be reactivated. `If-Match` is honored when supplied but not required. Returns the updated gym.

Reversible. The reason is required and is returned by the API — an operator lifting the suspension next week needs to know why it happened. `If-Match` is honored when supplied but not required. Returns the updated gym.

get.description: Each role reports the permissions it bundles and how many administrators hold it — the number to know before changing what a role grants.
System roles are seeded and their grants are reconciled to the code on every startup, so they are not editable through the API.
get.summary: One role and its permission grants

get.description: Paged and filterable. `search` matches email, first name, and last name; `status` filters on Active, Suspended, or PendingActivation. `pageSize` is capped server-side.

post.description: The account is created without a password, in PendingActivation, and cannot sign in until its owner sets one. No administrator ever sets another's password. Returns the created administrator and its `ETag`, so no follow-up GET is needed.

get.description: Returns the effective permission set alongside the roles that grant it.
get.summary: One administrator, with roles and resolved permissions

put.description: Email is not editable here — it is the login identity and the audit key. Requires `If-Match` carrying the `rowVersion` you read: without it the request is refused with 428, and a stale version with 409. Returns the updated administrator and its new `ETag`.

post.description: An account that never set a password returns to PendingActivation rather than becoming usable. `If-Match` is honored when supplied but not required. Returns the updated administrator.

put.description: Declarative: send the complete set. Refused for your own account, and refused when it would remove the role from the last active SuperAdmin. Requires `If-Match` carrying the `rowVersion` you read. Returns the updated administrator.

post.description: Rotates the security stamp and revokes every refresh token, so access ends immediately rather than at token expiry. Refused for your own account, and for the last active SuperAdmin. `If-Match` is honored when supplied but not required — the lifecycle transition rules already refuse the unsafe orderings. Returns the updated administrator.
post.summary: Suspend an administrator and end their sessions
